{{ElectionsOH}}
The '''2026 United States Senate special election in Ohio''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Ohio]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] appointee [[Jon Husted]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former senator [[Sherrod Brown]] are the respective nominees for their parties. The winner will complete the term won in [[2022 United States Senate election in Ohio|2022]] by [[JD Vance]], who resigned in 2025 to become vice president.

Seeking to keep the seat after his appointment, Husted ran unopposed for the Republican nomination. Brown, who represented Ohio in the Senate for three terms until his defeat in [[2024 United States Senate election in Ohio|2024]], won the Democratic nomination against minimal opposition.

This will be the first U.S. Senate special election in Ohio since [[1954 United States Senate special election in Ohio|1954]].

== Background ==
After voting for [[President Barack Obama]] in both [[2008 United States presidential election in Ohio|2008]] and [[2012 United States presidential election in Ohio|2012]], Ohio has trended increasingly Republican in subsequent years and is now considered a moderate to strong [[Red states and blue states|red state]] at the federal and state level. Republicans control all statewide offices, majorities in both chambers of the [[Ohio State Legislature|state legislature]], and hold both [[United States Senate|Senate]] seats. Republicans also have a majority of the state's [[United States House of Representatives|House]] delegation with ten seats compared to five for Democrats.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Grabar|first=Henry|date=November 13, 2018|title=Democrats Proved They Can Win Again in Michigan, Wisconsin, and Pennsylvania. Why Not Ohio?|url=https://slate.com/business/2018/11/why-ohio-may-not-swing-state.html|access-date=January 18, 2026|website=Slate Magazine|language=en}}</ref>

Republican nominee [[Donald Trump]] won Ohio in [[2016 United States presidential election in Ohio|2016]] and [[2020 United States presidential election in Ohio|2020]] by 8 percentage points, and in [[2024 United States presidential election in Ohio|2024]] grew his margin to 11 percentage points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schladen |first=Marty |date=2024-11-06 |title=Trump wins Ohio for a third time |url=https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2024/11/05/trump-wins-ohio-for-a-third-time-associated-press-projects/ |access-date=2024-12-05 |website=[[Ohio Capital Journal]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Additionally, Republican [[JD Vance]], now the [[Vice President of the United States|vice president of the United States]], defeated Democrat [[Tim Ryan (Ohio politician)|Tim Ryan]] in the [[2022 United States Senate election in Ohio|2022 U.S. Senate election]] by slightly over 6 points, while Republican [[Bernie Moreno]] defeated then-incumbent Sherrod Brown in the [[2024 United States Senate election in Ohio|2024 U.S. Senate election]] by slightly over 3.5 points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Nick |date=2024-11-06 |title=Republican Bernie Moreno defeats incumbent Sherrod Brown for Ohio U.S. Senate seat • Ohio Capital Journal |url=https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2024/11/05/republican-bernie-moreno-defeats-incumbent-sherrod-brown-for-ohio-u-s-senate-seat-ap-projects/ |access-date=2024-12-05 |website=[[Ohio Capital Journal]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Interim appointment==
According to Ohio law, if a U.S. Senate seat becomes vacant, the [[List of governors of Ohio|governor]] appoints a replacement who serves until December 15 following the next regularly scheduled statewide election that occurs more than 180 days after the vacancy. A special election to fill the remainder of the term is then held concurrently with that regular state election, which in this case would be the one on [[2026 Ohio elections|November 3, 2026]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Burd |first1=Aaron |title=How J.D. Vance's replacement in U.S. Senate will be picked if he becomes vice president |url=https://www.nbc4i.com/news/your-local-election-hq/how-j-d-vances-replacement-in-u-s-senate-will-be-picked-if-he-becomes-vice-president/ |work=[[WCMH-TV]] |date=July 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Filling vacancies in elective offices |url=https://www.ohiosos.gov/globalassets/elections/eoresources/general/fillingvacancies.pdf |publisher=Ohio Secretary of State |access-date=November 6, 2024 |page=2}}</ref> Governor [[Mike DeWine]] chose then-Lieutenant Governor Jon Husted to replace Vance in the Senate.

== General election ==
Data centers have become a major issue in the campaign, and a poll from [[Bowling Green State University]] showed 71% of Ohioans support a temporary ban on new construction of data centers. Brown has criticized Husted for his support of data centers in the past. As lieutenant governor from 2019 to 2025, Husted backed millions of dollars in tax breaks for data center construction projects in Ohio. Husted has defended data centers, saying they bring new jobs and money to rural areas. Husted has described data centers as a "local issue", and Brown has said that the approval of data centers should be decided on the local level.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sivaraman |first=Siddarth |date=August 10, 2026 |title=Ohio U.S. Senate candidates offer contrasting visions for data centers |url=https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2026/08/10/ohio-u-s-senate-candidates-offer-contrasting-visions-for-data-centers/ |access-date=September 29, 2026 |website=Ohio Capital Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

A September 2026 poll conducted by Bowling Green State University found that 25% of likely Ohio voters incorrectly believed Sherrod Brown was the incumbent U.S. senator from the state, despite him having lost re-election in 2024.<ref>{{cite news|last=Davines|first=Emily|date=September 28, 2026|title=In Ohio, a Humbling Question for Senator Jon Husted: Are You the Incumbent?|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/28/us/politics/john-husted-ohio-president-trump-midterms.html|url-access=subscription|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>
